study_identification_part.si4_title: Alzheimer's disease heterogeneity revealed by neuroanatomical normative modeling

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To apply neuroanatomical normative modeling using hierarchical Bayesian regression to a real-world clinical cohort of biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer's disease patients to assess intragroup neuroanatomical heterogeneity, explore anatomo-clinical correlations at an individual level, and examine the association between global amyloid burden and deviations in cortical thickness.

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Visual quality control performed independently by three authors (F.L., A.D., H.H.) with preliminary training for consistency. Errors found in 87 (82%) patients and 19 (68%) CN individuals. Most errors (75%) occurred at skull stripping step, leading to erroneous inclusion of dura/skull; fixed by adjusting parameters and/or manual brain mask editing. Remaining 25% of errors occurred at intensity normalization step; fixed by adding control points and/or manual WM voxel editing. After correction, recon-all was re-run and outputs re-inspected. Two patients excluded due to persistent segmentation errors after multiple correction attempts.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: Most errors occurred in the skull stripping step (75%) leading to the erroneous inclusion of portions of dura or skull within the pial surface... This type of error was fixed by adjusting input parameters to the skull stripping step and/or by manually editing the brain mask. The remaining 25% of errors occurred at the intensity normalization step... This type of error was fixed by adding control points to adjust voxel intensity and/or by manually adding/erasing WM voxels... At this stage, 2 patients had to be excluded due to persistent segmentation errors after multiple correction attempts, leaving a total of 104 patients. (Supplementary Fig.2 description)

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) with partial pooling was employed. Site-specific parameters are drawn from shared prior distributions with weakly informative hyperpriors (wide Gaussian). This approach enables compromise between complete pooling and no pooling, estimating distinct parameters for each batch/site while sharing information via common priors. The reference model was adapted using cortical thickness from 20 site-matched controls at ICHT through transfer learning, providing stable estimates of transferred model parameters. HBR calculates z-statistics accounting for both additive and multiplicative batch effects, avoiding the need for separate data harmonization (e.g., ComBat).
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: HBR is an effective means of addressing these limitations, primarily because it incorporates structural dependencies among model parameters by sharing a common prior distribution. In the context of HBR, it is assumed that parameters specific to each data collection site, which govern the data generation process, are drawn from the same prior distribution. To implement this assumption, a wide Gaussian distribution is employed as a weakly informative hyperprior over the parameters associated with the priors... HBR further enables a compromise between two extreme scenarios: complete pooling and no pooling... it calculates z-statistics to account for both additive and multiplicative batch effects, obviating the need for data harmonization. (Appendix 1)

nm1_model_origin.detail: Reference normative model trained on 33,072 healthy controls from multiple publicly available datasets (compiled by Kia and colleagues), using age and sex as covariates to model cortical thickness across 148 ROIs. The model was then adapted/recalibrated using transfer learning with cortical thickness data from 20 site-matched CN controls scanned at ICHT to provide stable estimates of transferred model parameters before generating z-scores for the clinical cohort. See Kia et al. (2022) and the reference study (Verdi et al.) for details on the original reference cohort compilation.
nm1_model_origin.supporting_text: Hierarchical Bayesian regression... was previously trained on the reference cohort (compiled by Kia and colleagues) consisting of a large sample of healthy controls who did not have any known clinical symptoms at the time of scanning, using age and sex as the covariates to index population variability in cortical thickness across all 148 regions of interest (ROIs)... This model was then optimized using cortical thickness data from controls scanned at the same acquisition site as the clinical cohort (n = 20). This gives stable estimates of the transferred model parameters in an adapted transfer learning approach. (L111-114). References cite Kia et al. 2022 (Ref 28) and Verdi et al. (Ref 24).

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Regional z-scores (cortical thickness deviation from normative range); Outliers defined as z < -1.96 (bottom 2.5% of normative distribution); Total outlier count (tOC) = sum of outlier regions per patient (range 0-148); Individual outlier maps visualizing spatial distribution of deviations.
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The methods section clearly defines the z-score threshold for outliers, the rationale for the threshold, and the calculation of total outlier count. Outlier maps are described as a visualization tool.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: This recalibrated model was then used to generate regional cortical thickness z-scores for each participant in the clinical cohort, relative to the normative range of the reference cohort... Here, z-scores of < -1.96 were defined as outliers, representing the bottom 2.5% of the normative range and indicating an extreme negative deviation of cortical thickness. This threshold has been adopted in similar studies... The total outlier count was calculated by summing the number of outlier regions for each patient... we built individualized outlier maps. (L111-122). The total outlier count ranges between 0 (no mapped regions are outliers) and 148 (all mapped regions are outliers). (L176-177)

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Statistical tests included: (1) ANCOVA with age and sex as covariates to test group effects (sex, phenotype, disease stage, depression history) on log-transformed total outlier count; (2) Pearson correlation between total outlier count and age; (3) ANOVA and Mann-Whitney tests for regional outlier percentages with Bonferroni correction; (4) Two-way ANOVA testing interaction between outlier location (temporal vs extratemporal) and phenotype; (5) Hamming distance matrices to quantify intragroup dissimilarity in outlier patterns; (6) Linear regression testing association between total outlier count and mean amyloid SUVR (with and without age covariate); (7) Standard case-control comparisons using ANCOVA for mean cortical thickness and region-level two-tailed t-tests with FDR correction between AD patients (n=79) and age/sex-matched ADNI controls (n=79).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Neuroanatomical heterogeneity in biomarker-confirmed AD is substantial, with the superior temporal sulcus most frequently affected; higher total outlier counts are associated with non-amnestic presentation, more advanced disease stage, female sex, and lower amyloid burden.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: In 86 biomarker-confirmed AD patients, median total outlier count was 21.5 (IQR=35, range 1-120 out of 148 ROIs). The superior temporal sulcus (STS) showed the highest outlier proportion in both hemispheres (left 52%, right 60%), with 48% showing bilateral STS outliers, 17% unilateral, and 35% no STS outliers. Patients with bilateral STS outliers were younger (mean 63.93±7.71 vs 71.11±6.31 years, F(2,83)=9.59, p<0.001), had lower mean cortical thickness (2.21±0.13 vs 2.38±0.093 mm, F(2,83)=21.31, p<0.001), more advanced disease (70.7% vs 40% dementia, χ²(2)=7.25, p=0.03), and more non-amnestic presentations (65.9% vs 6.7%, χ²(2)=8.72, p=0.01). Total outlier count was significantly higher in: (1) AD-dementia vs MCI-AD (median 30 vs 17.5, F(1,82)=8.33, p=0.005); (2) non-amnestic vs amnestic (median 37.5 vs 19.5, F(1,81)=5.49, p=0.02); (3) females vs males (median 31.5 vs 17.5, U=565, p=0.002); (4) patients without depression vs those with ongoing depression (median 30 vs 16, F(1,70)=8.56, p=0.005). Hamming distance analyses revealed substantial within-group dissimilarity (median=35.25, IQR=20.75), with greater dissimilarity in dementia vs MCI (median 41 vs 28, F(1,82)=8.15, p<0.01) and non-amnestic vs amnestic (median 44.75 vs 31.5, F(1,84)=8.13, p<0.01). Temporal regions showed higher outlier proportion than extratemporal (31.5±13.7% vs 19.1±10.5%, F(1,146)=29.39, p<0.001). Total outlier count was negatively associated with amyloid burden (SUVR) (p=0.01, R²=0.077) and this association survived age adjustment (p=0.02, R²=0.093). Mean cortical thickness was significantly lower in the clinical cohort vs age/sex-matched ADNI controls (2.29±0.13 vs 2.46±0.11, F(1,154)=88.78, p<0.001), with 104 of 148 regions significantly thinner after FDR correction.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The z<-1.96 threshold and total outlier count provide an interpretable individualized marker of heterogeneity that may have translational value for clinical decision-making. The case series (Figure 4) demonstrates practical application for investigating individual-level anatomo-clinical associations in patients with comparable clinical features but heterogeneous outlier profiles. Future studies could explore full z-score ranges rather than binary outliers, incorporate structural covariance between regions, consider spatial extent/magnitude within regions, and use connectivity-informed normative models. The study demonstrates advantages of normative modeling over standard case-control approaches in revealing intragroup variation masked by group averaging.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Relatively small clinical sample size (n=86), partly due to unavailability of eligible T1-weighted images in clinical scans and exclusions for quality issues. Scanner and field strength mismatch between clinical cohort (1.5T Siemens Avanto) and adaptation dataset (3T Siemens Verio) may contribute to unwanted noise in the model, though strict QC criteria were applied. Retrospective data collection limited availability of granular quantification of cognitive functioning (only screening measures ACE/MMSE available for case series) and depressive symptoms. APOE genotype and co-pathologies (e.g., vascular disease) were not available to examine their influence on heterogeneity. Subcortical structures were not included in the normative model, limiting comprehensive assessment of depression-atrophy associations. The method treats brain regions independently without considering structural covariance, which should be considered when interpreting Hamming distances and outlier maps. Spatial extent and magnitude of affected voxels within regions were not examined. Eighteen externally scanned patients were excluded by the model.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Full reference cohort dataset list from Supplementary Table 1: ABCD, Cam-CAN, CNP, FCON-1000, HCP, OASIS3, PNC, TOP, UK Biobank (9 datasets total). Of 256 amyloid-positive patients in the Imperial APC cohort scanned 2014-2021, 186 had MRI within 12 months of PET; 82 excluded for unavailable/ineligible T1 images, motion artifacts, other pathologies, or segmentation failure; 18 scanned externally were excluded by the model, leaving final n=86. FreeSurfer version 6.0 was used for the clinical cohort; Supplementary Table 1 shows reference datasets used FS v6.0 (table incomplete in materials). Adaptation dataset: 20 CN older adults scanned at ICHT on 3T Siemens Verio. Clinical cohort scanned at ICHT on 1.5T Siemens Avanto (86/104 included patients). Amyloid ligands: 18F-florbetapir (Amyvid) until Dec 2017, then 18F-florbetaben (Neuraceq). Amyloid quantification used Hermes BRASS v4.0 providing regional SUVR across 48 ROIs and global Aβ index. No explicit software package for implementing HBR normative modeling is stated (PCNtoolkit, Stan, PyMC not mentioned). No model performance metrics (EV, MSLL, skewness, kurtosis of z-scores) reported. Study is first application of neuroanatomical normative modeling with HBR to a real-world clinical AD cohort (previous work by Verdi et al. used ADNI research cohort). Depression definition from Petersen 2004 and Loreto 2022. MCI definition from Petersen 2004. Appropriate use criteria for amyloid PET from Johnson 2013. Analysis limited to negative deviations (atrophy) as primary interest was AD-related neurodegeneration.
